description:
First actual chaos. Kills processes inside a running peer cluster while the workload runs.

The whole fault schedule must be a pure function of {seed, config}. A failure is then a seed somebody else can run. This is the single most important property in the harness -- without it, a chaos failure is an anecdote.

Fault catalog for this child, weighted (processes die often):
- High: data-plane singletons -- commit proxy, resolver, sequencer, log server, materializer worker. These exercise the Director's monitor path, where any :DOWN other than the distributor is epoch-fatal and forces a fresh recovery.
- High: foreman-managed workers, exercising foreman restart.
- Medium: Director, non-leader Coordinator, Link.
- Low: leader Coordinator, forcing a Raft election plus Director re-recruitment.

Both brutal kills and graceful shutdowns -- bedrock_ex's evidence was that plain SIGTERM alone already produced {:shutdown, {:component_failure, ...}} and orphaned workers, so the graceful path is not the safe one.

Alongside: an append-only journal of every injected fault (timestamp, target role, pid, node, reason) interleaved with workload ops, flushed as it happens.

Note the spike's caveat: the peer's cluster tree is currently held by a parked spawn, so nothing supervises the root. If this child needs to observe the root dying, that owner becomes a monitored process first.

Whole-node faults are the next child; keep this one to in-node process kills.
title: Seeded fault scheduler and fault journal: process kills
